parsed.explanation: No traveler-facing criminalisation of trans identity/expression: Section 164 decriminalisation (2019, upheld 2021, deleted 2026) is operative. Residual Section 167 (female same-sex conduct) unrepealed — a secondary, undemonstrated lever against a trans woman. Social tolerance moderate (50% neighbour-tolerance, 2021), societal discrimination documented but dated (2011), implementation of court precedents rated 'unsatisfactory' (2024). No documented violence against trans people post-2011. No universal-exposure measures, border/document friction, or police targeting documented.

entry_documents.exposure: No border, document-mismatch, marker-recognition or screening friction is documented for visitors either way. Whether foreign documents are accepted without secondary scrutiny is an open question in the dossier.
entry_documents.protection: Constitutional dignity/privacy/equality rights held to cover trans people (2017 rulings) and 'sex' read generously (2019) supply a legal backdrop for any document dispute.
entry_documents.interaction: Open questions at entry feed into a court system that has demonstrably granted trans litigants relief, but entry practice itself is not sourced.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: No documented arrest, detention or custody practice targeting trans visitors. Section 167 remains unrepealed for women and its reach over a trans woman's relationships is unresolved — a latent, undocumented lever rather than an enforced one.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Decriminalisation operative; police historically 'did not target same-sex activity' (2011); courts voided the morality provision as inviting police intrusion.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A latent statute plus unresolved Section 167 status could in principle be used by an officer, but no enforcement record exists.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No facility, ward, custody-placement or bathroom restriction is documented at any level of government. No subnational variation is recorded; urban/rural policing and tolerance differences are unsourced.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Constitutional inhuman-and-degrading-treatment clause applied in trans litigation; national-level findings apply uniformly.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Absence of documented facility rules leaves this axis open; the national framing means no protective subnational regime exists to compensate either.

care_services.exposure: No documented denial of care, medication seizure or ward misplacement for trans visitors. Insurance, hormone-refill and emergency-care treatment are not sourced.
care_services.protection: Registered national LGBTIQ+ organisation runs health/HIV services and support resources; constitutional non-discrimination reasoning applies to services.
care_services.interaction: Community infrastructure can backstop a visitor turned away by a public facility, though its reach for foreigners is not documented.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Mixed official signals: a 2011 deputy speaker's kill remark (dated, single official, no adoption), community groups calling the 2019 appeal 'homophobia and transphobia.' Dated rhetoric with no institutional follow-through.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: President deported an anti-gay pastor (2016), acknowledged violations and deserved protection (2018); courts criticised morality policing; employment act covers sexual orientation since 2010.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Protective executive statements plus working courts outweigh the dated legislative remark; no state campaign or threat-framing policy exists.

minors_guardians.exposure: No documented rule, custody practice or service refusal affecting a trans adult travelling with a minor. Family-visiting and guardianship-specific risks are unsourced.
minors_guardians.protection: Constitutional equality and non-discrimination reasoning would apply to a parent-child case; no hostility toward trans guardians is recorded.
minors_guardians.interaction: Nothing in the dossier shows a minor's presence triggering additional scrutiny.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Societal discrimination documented (2011) and neighbour tolerance only 50% (2021), implying friction and possible service refusals. No post-2011 violence data exists — absence of evidence, not evidence of safety.
street_violence_police_response.protection: No reported SOGI-based violence (2011); functioning police and courts; registered advocacy organisation; presidential condemnation of hate speech.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Moderate tolerance with functioning institutions caps ordinary social friction at discomfort rather than threat, but recency gaps keep this axis partly open.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Regional litigation body rates implementation of the country's own precedents 'unsatisfactory' (2024); no administrative gender-recognition route exists (resident-facing, not traveler exposure); Section 167 and post-2011 violence data unresolved.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Courts have twice delivered trans litigants binding wins, government issued the ID card after abandoning its appeal, constitutional complaint route is proven to work.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies exist and have operated for trans claimants, but slow executive implementation means redress is real yet delayed — a partial offset, not a guarantee.

anchor_checks.comparison: Far above: no entry bar, register, exclusion or discretionary refusal regime exists for trans visitors here. Dossier documents no traveler-facing administrative sanction of any kind, whereas 0.35-A's defining feature is routine, universally applied exclusion with no remedy.

Comparable tier: 0.65-A pairs documented friction (stop, intrusive questioning) with national protections that operate and a remedy that produced apology and compensation. This dossier has comparable protections operating but no documented incident at all — fewer negatives, but also thinner evidence of friction and a dated tolerance figure, holding it near this level.

Slightly below: 0.75-C documents trained border officers, recognized markers, and a tribunal that secures release and compensation. Here border practice is entirely unsourced and social tolerance is only 50%, so the traveller lacks the documented entry-stage assurances that anchor 0.75-C's higher score.

parsed.synthesis: The combined operative regime is decriminalised, constitutionally protective and litigated rather than legislated. Section 164 is gone from the statute book; courts have granted trans people binding constitutional victories and the government complied on the ID card; a registered national organisation provides infrastructure; executive statements are broadly protective. Against that: Section 167 remains for women (latent, secondary, no enforcement record), neighbour tolerance is 50%, discrimination evidence is dated (2011), implementation of precedents is rated unsatisfactory (2024), and virtually every traveler-facing axis — border documents, facilities, care, minors — is simply unsourced. That combination — working courts, no universal exposure, no documented targeting, moderate society, thin visitor data — sits in Reduced Risk, below the trained-border-officer tier but well above anchors with administrative exclusion.
